scholarships.title: Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships
scholarships.official_source: Alberta Innovates (Government of Alberta provincial agency), delivered through participating Alberta post-secondary institutions

eligibility: Be a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident of Canada, or an international student.

Be enrolled as a full-time graduate student conducting full-time research at one of the participating institutions: Athabasca University, Concordia University of Edmonton, the University of Alberta, the University of Calgary or the University of Lethbridge.
Be conducting research in a key emerging technology area of information and communications technologies (ICT) or advanced materials and manufacturing technologies (AMM).

Be able to clearly articulate how your research aligns with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and how your research can produce potential environmental, health, economic, social and other impacts for Alberta.
At the University of Calgary: be applying to, or enrolled in, a thesis-based graduate degree programme.
At the University of Calgary: have submitted your admissions application and received your University of Calgary student number (UCID).
Meet the eligibility requirements in the terms of reference of the award at the time the award is paid, even if you did not meet them at the time you applied.
existing.eligibility_summary: Canadian, permanent resident or international graduate students conducting full-time research in information and communications technologies or advanced materials and manufacturing technologies at one of the five named participating Alberta post-secondary institutions, whose project develops rather than merely uses an emerging technology and who can articulate its potential impact for Alberta.
benefits: Scholarship funding enabling full-time graduate students to devote their full time to their academic studies
Published range of $12,000 to $31,000 per year, with terms of one to four years
At the University of Calgary: $26,000 for master's students for up to two years and $31,000 for doctoral students for up to four years

AGES top-up value of $18,000, available only to students who have applied for and been awarded both an Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarships award and an Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships award
Major Award top-up value of $12,000, available only to students who have applied for and been awarded both a major award and an Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships award

requirements: Check with your institution's faculty of graduate studies for full descriptions and application details.
Submit your application to your institution; the applicant does not apply directly to Alberta Innovates.
At the University of Calgary: submit your admissions application and obtain your UCID before applying for the award.

At the University of Calgary: go to your Student Centre and click the link Apply for Graduate Funding in the Financial Aid section of your home screen, then select the Graduate Award Competition Application.
Only one application is required regardless of the number of awards you are applying for.
You may create one application per competition each year; if an application is incorrectly cancelled you must contact your graduate program to request reactivation.
Request and track your references before finalizing your application so they arrive before or by the application deadline.
New students can use their references from their admission application toward their scholarship application.

Reference letters used for admission may be used toward the scholarship competition as long as they were written within the eleven months prior to the Faculty of Graduate Studies' February 1 deadline.
Transcripts will be uploaded to the application by your program; scholarship requirements may differ from admission requirements.
Awards are based on merit; read and understand the terms of reference.
documents: Up-to-date transcript, uploaded to the application by your program
Reference letters, requested and tracked through the Student Awards Application
University of Calgary student number (UCID), obtained through the admissions application
Terms of reference review, which is a required preparation step rather than a submitted document
application_method: Check with your institution's faculty of graduate studies for the full description and application details.
Submit your application to your institution.
Wait for your application to be reviewed by that institution.
existing.selection_notes: Selection is institution-specific. Each of the participating Alberta institutions has its own scholarship application and evaluation processes for students in full-time programmes, and Alberta Innovates directs students to their faculty of graduate studies for that information. At the University of Calgary the competition is merit-based and the applicant must be able to clearly articulate alignment with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and the potential impacts of the work for Alberta. For the Killam and Open Doctoral categories a first-class average is required, which at the University of Calgary is a grade point average of 3.5 or higher in the last two years of study, though that published indicator is stated for those categories rather than for the Alberta Innovates category. Successful students may normally hold one GAC scholarship per year across the Open Doctoral and Special Awards categories and will be awarded the highest-value scholarship for which they are eligible.
existing.best_fit: Master's or doctoral students, including international students, enrolled full time in a thesis-based research programme at the University of Alberta, University of Calgary, University of Lethbridge, Athabasca University or Concordia University of Edmonton, whose research develops an Applied Digital or Emerging Technology in natural sciences or engineering and can produce potential environmental, health, economic and social impacts for Alberta.
existing.notes: Multi-year scholarships are renewed annually after the first year upon satisfactory reporting by the student. Students who have been awarded an Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarship must complete annual and final reports through the term of their award, and post-award reports after the end of the award. No deferral rule, no return-home obligation and no clinical or practice-location restriction are published. You may create only one application per competition each year. At the University of Calgary, students in course-based and professional degree programs are NOT eligible for the Graduate Award Competition through which this award is applied for.
existing.duration: Terms vary from one to four years, depending on the recipient's time in the program. At the University of Calgary the published terms are $26,000 for master's students for up to two years and $31,000 for doctoral students for up to four years.
existing.application_period: Continuous at the funder level, with a seasonal intake at each institution. Alberta Innovates publishes the due date as "Continuous". At the University of Calgary the Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 each year, program deadlines vary and must be confirmed with Graduate Program Staff, and results for the Alberta Innovates competition are announced September to December. Awards are paid in the following academic year, with the majority starting in September.
existing.deadline_display: No single calendar deadline is published. The Alberta Innovates programme page gives the due date as "Continuous" and states "This program is accepting applications on a seasonal basis. Intake Open Date is specific to each individual university; please contact your university of choice for deadline information." At the University of Calgary, "The Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 of each year" and "Deadlines vary by program"; the Faculty of Graduate Studies reference deadline is February 1.
